## MVC (Model-View-Controller)

- **Model**: Contains all business logic, data access, and validation — this is the "fat" layer that encapsulates domain knowledge.
- **View**: Responsible only for presentation and rendering — **NEVER** put business logic, data transformation, or formatting decisions in Views.
- **Controller**: Thin orchestration layer that receives requests, delegates to Models/Services, and selects the appropriate View — **NEVER** put business logic in Controllers.
- Keep Controllers focused on a single resource or workflow — one Controller per domain concept.
- **NEVER** access the database or call external services directly from Controllers — always delegate to the Model or Service layer.
- Use dependency injection to provide Models and Services to Controllers — **NEVER** instantiate them manually inside controller methods.
- Prefer "skinny Controllers, fat Models" — if a Controller method exceeds 10 lines of logic, extract it into the Service/Model layer.
